packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-03 - unverified image-only reading

Exposure: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this item. Feast and saint names below are transcribed because they are written on the leaf.
Beyond the rules: to read the small pasted slip on face 2 (only partly inside the tiles), I made a 3x upscaled crop of that area of image-010 in my own scratchpad. No other file was opened.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- Two faces, each with one overview: image-001 (face 1) with tiles image-002..009 (2 across x 4 down, overlapping); image-010 (face 2) with tiles image-011..018 (same grid).
- Face 1 (image-001): parchment leaf at the front of the volume, against the board. A later printed-border paper label with "1695." in ink at upper left; a parchment strip/stub and a patch at left and lower left. Main content: one column of short entries, each starting "De ..." with a red touch on the initial, each followed by a reference made of a letter (a, b) and a number. At the bottom the column splits: a second short list starts at mid-page right, joined by a brace/vertical stroke. Red and black ruled lines separate the "a" and "b" groups. A drawn stroke runs down the left of the list (a bar/frame line), with a small rosette at its top.
- On face 1 a much fainter, larger, older script shows through or survives (ghost/erased text or offset) in the upper and right areas, under and beside the list. It looks like a different, earlier text in a bigger book hand. I did not read it.
- Face 1 left margin (image-004, image-006): a group of short later cursive notes on the stub/strip, separated by ruled strokes, in a small hand, apparently not Latin in every case (one looks German: "gelassen"?).
- Face 2 (image-010): two columns of the same kind of list, ruled frame in ink, red strokes on initials and red underlines; references now use letters b, c, d, e. Ends in a drawn scroll/banderole "Finis tabule". A small pasted parchment slip with 13 short lines of cursive at upper right; below it the board shows a strip of another manuscript (pastedown/turn-in) with lines of small text, illegible.
- Interpretation (tentative): a table of contents of sermons for feasts and topics, keyed to quire letters plus leaf numbers. The text proper is not on these faces.

NUMERAL FORMS: The numbers use late-medieval arabic shapes. I read: loop-shaped half-8 = 4; a hooked "y/ч" shape = 6 (?) or 5 (?); an inverted-V "Λ" = 7; a "z" shape = 2; a "ꝁ/le"-like shape after 1 = 5 (?), so "1ꝁ" = 15 (?). Wherever the shape is not certain I give the value with "?". Check numerals against the images before using them.

UNREAD / LIMITATIONS
- Not read: the faint older script under/around the list on face 1 (image-003, image-005, image-007 right halves); the manuscript strip on the board at right of face 2 (image-010, x c. 1120-1300, y c. 560-1500), which is outside the tiles except at their edges; most of the face-1 margin notes.
- Numerals are the weakest part. Several letter+number refs are overwritten or corrected.
- Repeated lines in overlapping tiles (e.g. "De eadem a 3" in image-003 and image-005; "In cena domini e 8 . 9" in image-016 and image-018) were counted once.
- Suggested additional views: native tiles of the slip and of the board strip on face 2; a raking-light or UV view of face 1 for the underlying text.
